subject: Music and Dance

source.title: Senior School Curriculum Design — Music and Dance, Grade 10 (2025 draft)
source.notes: Full 60-page PDF text extracted directly via the Read tool (no `pages` param) from a user-supplied file ('download (5).pdf', copied to grade 10 desings/Grade10-MusicAndDance-SeniorSchool.pdf). Watermarked DRAFT throughout — this is Kenya's first-ever Grade 10 (Senior School) curriculum design, not yet finalized. Strand/sub-strand text transcribed verbatim, including all parenthetical enumerations, per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Rhythm
keyConcepts: Semi-quaver
Triplet
Simple time: 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 and 3/8
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the rhythmic concept of the semiquaver in simple time
Describe the concept of the triplet in simple time
Group notes into beats in simple time
Compose 4-bar rhythms in simple time incorporating semiquavers
Compose 4-bar rhythms in simple time incorporating triplets
Appreciate rhythms composed by self and others
keyInquiryQuestions: How do triplets feature in simple time?
How can rhythms be created in simple time?
learningExperiences: Listen to or sing songs in simple time with semiquavers and aurally recognize them in the songs
Use virtual sources responsibly to listen to or sing songs in simple time with triplets and discuss the performance of the triplet
Practice writing rhythms in simple time incorporating semiquavers with appropriate grouping
Tap and recite rhythms using French rhythm names
Collaboratively discuss factors to consider in creating rhythmic patterns and apply them to create 4-bar rhythms
Compose 4-bar original rhythms in simple time incorporating semiquavers and triplets
Perform created rhythms in simple time and record using a digital device, observing responsibility
Share the recorded performances of rhythms with peers for critique
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Cyber security (responsible use of digital devices/online platforms researching, recording, sharing)
Life skills (improvising rhythmic accompaniments to simple tunes)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric 'Ability to create works of Music and Dance' names '4-bar rhythms incorporating semiquavers' and '4-bar rhythms incorporating triplets' as separate, individually-graded items — both must be practiced as distinct compositions, not merged into one.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Melody in Major Keys
keyConcepts: Melodic devices: Scalic motion, Arpeggios
Major scales of D, A, B flat and E flat on the treble and bass staves, with and without key signatures, ascending and descending
Structure (question and answer phrases)
Articulation marks: slur, staccato
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe melodic devices used in melody writing
Construct major scales on a staff
Compose an 8-bar melody incorporating melodic devices
Compose an 8-bar melody incorporating articulation marks
Enjoy creating melodies in major keys
keyInquiryQuestions: How is melodic interest created in music?
How can unity and variety be achieved in composition?
learningExperiences: Listen to or sing simple and familiar tunes in major keys and identify melodic devices used
Construct major scales on the treble and bass staves ascending and descending
Compose 8-bar melodies in simple time incorporating melodic devices with appropriate phrasing
Compose 8-bar melodies in simple time incorporating articulation marks
Sing or play composed melodies
Store composed music in a digital or physical portfolio
Critique melodies composed by self and others
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Cyber security (responsible use of digital apps)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric requires '8-bar melodies' and 'set melody to text' and 'second part to a melody' as separately-graded 'works of Music and Dance' items — melodic devices and articulation marks are each graded outcomes, not optional flourishes.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Transposition
keyConcepts: Intervals: Melodic and harmonic, quality (Major, minor, perfect) and size — 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8ve
Transposition to an interval — 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 8ve
Transposition from treble to bass staves and vice versa
To a given key — C, G, F, D, A, B flat and E flat
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe intervals in a major scale
Explain the concept of transposition in music
Transpose music to a given interval
Transpose music from the treble to the bass staff
Transpose music from bass to the treble staff
Transpose music to a given key
Value the role of transposition in music
keyInquiryQuestions: How does transposition aid in music performance?
learningExperiences: Sing or play a major scale and aurally identify various intervals
Listen to melodies sung or played in octaves and identify the lower and higher registers
Sing or play melodies at different pitches, higher or lower, to distinguish the difference in pitch
Discuss the process of transposing music to a given interval, an octave or a given key
Transpose melodies an octave up or down within the same or to a different stave
Transpose melodies to a given key within the same or to a different stave
scopeNotes: notes: The design's printed 'Core competencies to be developed' / Values / PCIs block immediately following this sub-strand's table (p.21) reads as generic composition/notation-software text ('creates new musical ideas when composing melodies in the minor key', 'applies compositional skills and knowledge on digital software to compose and notate music', 'uses music notation software to compose and playback music') rather than text specific to transposition, intervals, or major keys — this sub-strand names no minor key at all. Likely a copy/paste artifact in this still-DRAFT document (shared boilerplate reused across nearby sub-strands). Recorded verbatim per mining discipline; treated as low-confidence for this sub-strand specifically and NOT used to justify building a minor-key or notation-software branch inside the Transposition skill — those belong to 1.2/1.6 instead.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Cyber security (responsible use of digital apps)
Self-esteem (belief in self as upcoming artiste through melody-writing knowledge)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric 'Ability to transpose music' grades three distinct skills separately: 'From treble to bass', 'From bass to treble', 'To a given key' — all three directions must be practiced, not just one.

subStrands.name: 1.4 Setting Text to Music
keyConcepts: Process of setting text to music: syllabic division, accents (strong and weak), natural speech inflection/intonation of words, rhythm, time signature, cadential points and pitch
Two lines of text (8 syllables for each phrase)
Downbeat and upbeat (Anacrusis) start of melodies

Kiswahili text on: Regulations for road users (Observe designated crossing points and use of Personal Protective Equipment), financial literacy (self financial management skills), waste management, drug and substance abuse, healthy relationships
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline the process of setting text in Kiswahili to music
Set a melody to text in Kiswahili
Appreciate music composed in Kiswahili by self and others
keyInquiryQuestions: How are pitches assigned to different words to communicate messages clearly?
How does text dictate composition of a melody?
learningExperiences: Discuss the process involved in setting text in Kiswahili to music
Read Kiswahili words to establish the accents, natural speech inflections, and intonation
Discuss factors that guide syllabic division and accentuation of text in Kiswahili
Select text in Kiswahili on pertinent and contemporary issues such as: regulation for road users, financial literacy, waste management, drug and substance abuse, healthy relationships
Recite the text to establish the text-melody relationships: natural speech inflections, intonation and textual meaning among others
Choose an appropriate time signature, assign note values, identify cadential points and phrases for the selected text
Add appropriate pitches to the syllables while paying attention to word painting, melodic contour, range and overall structure
Write the music composed in staff notation
Organize a concert and perform the composed song to the school or local community audience
Record and save the music in a digital or physical portfolio
linkedLearningAreas: Implied bridge to Kiswahili — the sub-strand's text-setting content is built entirely from Kiswahili-language text, though no formal 'Link to other learning area' box is printed for this design.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Waste management (sensitizing community on environmental cleanliness)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric grades 'Set melody to text' as its own item under 'Ability to create works of Music and Dance' — separate from the 8-bar melody and second-part items, confirming text-setting is assessed as a standalone composition skill.

subStrands.name: 1.5 Two-Part Harmony
keyConcepts: Two-part harmony guidelines: Beginning (unison, 5ths or 8ve); Motion — step, leap, note-to-note
Intervals (consonants: major 3rd, minor 3rd, perfect 4th, perfect 5th, major 6th, minor 6th, and the octave)
Ending — unison or 8ve
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline guidelines for creating two-part harmony
Compose a second part to a 4-bar melody in a major key
Value the role of intervals in harmony
keyInquiryQuestions: What do you consider when adding a second part to an existing melody?
How can intervals be utilized in improvising a second part to a melody?
learningExperiences: Listen to two-part vocal and/or instrumental harmonic passages in major keys to identify guidelines used in two-part harmony
Sing and/or play two-part harmonic passages in major keys to aurally discriminate the higher and lower parts in the passages
Distinguish harmonic intervals as consonant or dissonant
Add a second part above or below a melody using appropriate consonant intervals
Score two-part harmonic passages on the treble stave with appropriate stemming
Record the 2-part music using a digital device or a physical portfolio
Appraise each other's music
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric grades 'Second part to a melody' as its own composition item, and lists all 7 consonant intervals under 'Ability to describe Music and Dance concepts' — a skill must be able to name/identify all 7 (major 3rd, minor 3rd, perfect 4th, perfect 5th, major 6th, minor 6th, octave), not a subset.

subStrands.name: 1.6 Music Notation Software
keyConcepts: Navigate music notation software — opening, keying, playing back, saving, and editing
Transcribe scales, melodies, intervals and two-part harmony
Saving — midi, print, and audio formats
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify notation software used in music writing
Navigate selected music notation software
Transcribe music using a music notation software
Save music files for storage
Appreciate music playbacks in midi and audio formats
keyInquiryQuestions: How is music notation software useful?
How does music notation software facilitate music composition?
learningExperiences: Watch demos of various music notation software to distinguish them
Discuss various notation software and mobile apps used in music notation
Navigate selected music notation software to view music notation tools
Use music notation software to key in music
Edit keyed-in music using a selected music software
Save and convert already keyed in music to midi, print, and audio formats
Share, play back, and appraise own and others' music in print and audio formats
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Safety and security (precaution using digital devices powered by electricity)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric 'Ability to use music notation software' grades three sub-skills separately: 'Navigate software', 'Transcribe music', 'Save music files' — a skill needs all three, not just navigation.

subStrands.name: 1.7 Dance Production
keyConcepts: Elements of dance — Body, Action, Space, Time, Energy
Functions of costumes, props and set design
Design of costumes
Multimedia
Choice of Music, lighting and sound effects

Choose a dance theme based on a PCI: Risk awareness and management on road use (Risky road behaviours such as: speeding, racing, running while on the road, jay walking, creating awareness on the vices of looting from crashed vehicles such as tankers, beverage transporters and from victims of a crash)
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the elements of dance
Improvise props for use in a dance performance
Design costumes based on a dance theme
Describe the concept of choreography in a themed dance
Select multimedia effects for use in a dance production
Value dance production for economic empowerment
keyInquiryQuestions: How can costumes and props be used to communicate the theme in a dance performance?
How can multimedia effects be utilized to enhance dance production?
learningExperiences: Watch a variety of dances and discuss the elements of dance
Source or use available materials to improvise props for use in a dance performance
Choose a dance based on a theme of risk awareness and management on road use
Design an appropriate costume for the dance
Watch online or live demonstrations on use of music, lighting, and sound effects in a dance production
Apply multimedia effects in production of a dance performance during a school event
scopeNotes: notes: The printed 'Core competencies/Values/PCIs' block for this sub-strand (p.30) reads as text about recording/playing Kenyan popular music with digital audio apps, which more naturally matches Strand 2.0's Contemporary Dance sub-strand than 1.7's own elements-of-dance/costume/multimedia content. Likely another copy/paste artifact in this DRAFT design (same pattern noted for 1.3). Recorded verbatim; the road-safety PCI (risky road behaviours) is the one piece of this block that is unambiguously specific to 1.7 and IS used for scenario content.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Road safety (dance theme based on risk awareness and management on road use, appropriate costume design)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0 rubric grades 'Props and costumes' as its own item under 'Ability to create works of Music and Dance' — improvised props and designed costumes are each individually assessed outputs.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Kenyan Folk Songs
keyConcepts: Characteristics of Kenyan folksongs
Folksongs — Solo, Group
Choice — Gender, Age, Occasion, Costumes props and artefacts
Performance aspects — Singing (tone and diction), Idiom, Synchrony, Transitions, Instrumentation, Projection, Expressiveness, Etiquette
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the characteristics of Kenyan folk songs
Select a Kenyan folk song for performance
Perform folk songs from Kenyan communities applying performance aspects
Enjoy performing Kenyan folk songs
keyInquiryQuestions: How does exposure to various performances influence an individual's response to folk songs?
Why are Kenyan folk songs important in society?
learningExperiences: Listen to or watch performances of Kenyan folk songs and discuss the characteristics
Source from virtual or physical spaces to select Kenyan folk songs with appropriate themes and messages from different communities
Source for and select instruments, costumes, props, and artefacts, make-up and décor
Take up different roles in the performance (soloist, instrumentalists, group singers)

Record and share the performances with peers for feedback
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 2.0 rubric 'Ability to perform selected works of Music and Dance' grades 'A Kenyan folk song' as one of 5 individually-assessed performance items, using appropriate performance techniques and/or observing prescribed performance directions.

subStrands.name: 2.2 Western Style Solo Songs
keyConcepts: Performance style
Accuracy — pitch, rhythm
Performance directions — tempo, dynamics, repeats and reiterations
Performance techniques — phrasing, posture, diction, poise, and musicianship
Western solo songs: lieder, arias, folk songs
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the performance style of selected Western solo songs
Perform a Western style solo song using appropriate performance techniques
Perform a Western style solo song observing prescribed performance directions

keyInquiryQuestions: How should one prepare to perform a Western solo song?
Why are vocal techniques important in Western solo songs?
learningExperiences: Listen to or watch live or recorded performances of lieder, arias from operas and oratorios, and solo songs from musicals for familiarization
Discuss the performance practice of Western solo songs such as lieder, arias, and folk songs
Review videos of Western solo songs to identify their styles of singing
Execute various vocal styles applied in singing Western solo songs
Select, acknowledging the source, suitable Western solo songs for performance
Perform selected Western solo songs before a given audience, while observing the performance techniques

Evaluate performances by self and others and respectfully give feedback
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 2.0 rubric grades 'A Western solo song' as one of 5 individually-assessed performance items.

subStrands.name: 2.3 Kenyan Indigenous Musical Instrument (Solo Performer)

What features of a solo instrument mark its cultural identity?

Familiarise with a selected Kenyan indigenous musical instrument to identify its parts and handling

Practice the techniques of tuning of the instrument

Record and share music with parents, guardians, and fellow learners for feedback and upload to a digital portfolio
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 2.0 rubric grades 'Indigenous Kenyan instrument' as one of 5 individually-assessed performance items.

subStrands.name: 2.4 Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer)
keyConcepts: Western Instruments: strings, brass, woodwind, and percussion, piano/organ
Playing techniques: tonguing, bowing, picking, strumming, plucking, and striking
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the structure of the western solo instrument

Play a selected Western solo musical instrument observing performance directions

Tune or explain the tuning of a selected Western solo instrument

Play a variety of solo pieces of music on a selected solo instrument during a school function

subStrands.name: 2.5 Contemporary Dance from Kenya

Basic Performing Skills: Posture, Alignment, Balance, Coordination, Control
Performance techniques: Controlled leg work, Floor work, Improvisation, Fall and recovery, Movement and release
Dance Choreography based on Kenyan popular music (such as rhumba, benga, genge, hip-hop, Kenyan rock, genge tone, taarab, rap, and kapuka)

Choose a dance theme based on risk awareness and management on road use: Risky road behaviours such as over speeding, racing, running while on the road, jay walking, creating awareness on the vices of looting from crashed vehicles such as tankers, beverage transporters, and from victims of a crash
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the features of a contemporary dance
Create a 3-5-minute contemporary dance routine based on Kenyan popular music
Execute basic performance skills in a dance routine
Perform a 3-5-minute contemporary dance routine applying performance techniques
Appreciate performing a contemporary dance as a means of self-expression
keyInquiryQuestions: How can contemporary dance be used to tell a story?
learningExperiences: Watch real or virtual contemporary dance performances and discuss their features
Brainstorm an idea on a PCI (risk awareness and management on road use) for a dance story
Create milestones for the contemporary dance story based on risk awareness and management on road use
Demonstrate basic performance skills in a dance routine
Select suitable contemporary dance techniques and styles from genres of Kenyan popular music for the routine
Block dance movements and patterns for effective use of time, space, action, and energy

pertinentContemporaryIssues: Road safety (milestones for the contemporary dance story based on risk awareness and management of road use)

Ethnic and racial relations (acquainted with diverse dance techniques in various ethnic and racial cultures, nurtures respect for varied cultures of the world)

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 2.0 rubric grades 'A 3-5-minute contemporary dance routine' as one of 5 individually-assessed performance items, applying performance techniques and/or observing performance directions with 'expert precision' at the top band.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Kenyan Folk Songs
keyConcepts: Performance Media — vocal, vocal and instrumental
Performance styles — solo, call-response, choral

How can folk songs be used to address issues in the community?

Discuss the role of performance media and the various players in Kenyan folk songs
Identify the styles of Kenyan folk songs performance
Discuss how the elements of music feature in various Kenyan folk songs performances

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 3.0 rubric names 'Characteristics of Kenyan folk songs' under 'describes 3 aspects of Critical Appreciation' and 'Kenyan folk songs' under 'analyses 3 works of Music and Dance' — this sub-strand is graded on BOTH description and analysis, the two highest Bloom's verbs the outcomes explicitly use ('examine', 'analyse', 'evaluate').

subStrands.name: 3.2 Classical Music (Medieval and Renaissance)
keyConcepts: Periods — Medieval, Renaissance
Genres in Medieval period — Plain song, Organum, Motet
Genres in Renaissance period — Motet, Madrigal, Mass, Toccata, Canzona
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the characteristics of music genres in the prescribed periods
Aurally identify music genres in the prescribed period
Appreciate Medieval and Renaissance music through listening and analysis
keyInquiryQuestions: How does exposure to genres of music from the prescribed period influence an individual's response to music?
How does the characteristics of a historical period influence the music genre?
learningExperiences: Listen to and discuss the characteristics of music genres in the prescribed periods
Discuss the influences of the characteristic of the period on the features of the music
Responsibly search for, listen to, and aurally identify the prescribed music genres of the different periods by outlining the composer and the features of music
Develop informed personal responses to music of the prescribed periods
scopeNotes: notes: 'Motet' is explicitly listed in BOTH the Medieval genre list and the Renaissance genre list — this is a real, deliberate curriculum point (the motet genre spans and evolves across both periods), not a transcription duplicate. A comparison-tier question contrasting the Medieval motet against the Renaissance motet is directly sanctioned by this dual listing.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Online safety (responsible use of digital devices to search for genres of music)
Self-esteem (gains confidence performing music before an audience)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 3.0 rubric groups 'Sounds of Kenyan indigenous musical instruments' and 'Structure/Tuning of the Western solo instrument' and 'Features of a contemporary dance' alongside this sub-strand's genres under one combined 'describes 3 aspects' item — but 'Classical music (Medieval and Renaissance)' is also separately named under 'analyses 3 works', confirming both a description AND analysis pass is expected, matching the Understand+Analyze outcome verbs.

subStrands.name: 3.3 Music and Dance in Socio-cultural Context
keyConcepts: Functions — Religious, Social, Educational, Economic, Cultural
Changing musical practices (such as timing, language, costume and make-up, age of performers, audience, packaging of messages, collaborations, instrumentation, handling of props, and dance movements)
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the functions of Music and Dance in society
Examine the changing Music and Dance performance practices in different contexts
Value the functions of Music and Dance in society
keyInquiryQuestions: How does music influence the society?
How do various contexts influence music performances?
learningExperiences: Listen to, or watch performances of music in various contexts and discuss its functions
Discuss the changing musical practices in different performance settings
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Stress management (performs music whose therapeutic nature helps manage stress and emotions)
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 3.0 rubric names 'Functions of Music and Dance' under 'describes 3 aspects of Critical Appreciation' and 'Music and Dance in socio-cultural context' under 'analyses 3 works' — plus this is the ONE sub-strand across the whole design naming 'Critical thinking and Problem solving' as a core competency, which per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md mandates at least one Analyze-or-Evaluate-tier branch.

crossCuttingNotes: This design has NO 'Link to other learning area' boxes anywhere in its 3 strands (unlike e.g. Grade 7 Integrated Science) — the one exception is 1.4 Setting Text to Music, which is built entirely around Kiswahili-language text (an implicit, not formally boxed, cross-subject bridge).

Two sub-strands (1.3 Transposition, 1.7 Dance Production) have a printed Core Competencies/Values/PCIs block that reads as topically mismatched to their own SLO/learning-experience content — flagged individually in each sub-strand's scopeNotes above. Both are recorded verbatim per mining discipline; treated as low-confidence signal for content-shaping purposes.

Kenyan-context localization is structural to this subject, not decorative: 2.1/2.3/3.1 name Kenyan folk songs and indigenous instruments explicitly; 2.5 names 8 real Kenyan popular-music genres (rhumba, benga, genge, hip-hop, Kenyan rock, genge tone, taarab, rap, kapuka) as the required choreography source material — these are a hard content-breadth floor for the Contemporary Dance skill, not example filler.

Road safety (risky road behaviours: over-speeding, racing, running on the road, jay-walking, looting from crashed vehicles) is a repeated, explicit PCI across TWO sub-strands (1.7 Dance Production, 2.5 Contemporary Dance) — both must build a dance-theme scenario branch around this same named PCI, not invent a different theme.
No 'hazard'/exclusion notes ('avoid...') appear anywhere in this design — no content is explicitly deferred to a later grade within Music and Dance.
